about.title: About Timestamp Converter
about.description: The Timestamp Converter converts between human-readable dates and Unix timestamps (epoch time). Essential for developers, system administrators, and anyone working with databases, APIs, or log files that use timestamp formats. Supports bidirectional conversion with multiple timestamp formats including seconds and milliseconds since epoch, making it invaluable for debugging, data analysis, and system integration tasks.

faq.q: What is a Unix timestamp and how does it work?
faq.a: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds (or milliseconds) that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC, also known as the Unix epoch. Our timestamp converter handles both formats for accurate date-time conversions.

faq.q: How do I know if my timestamp is in seconds or milliseconds?
faq.a: Timestamps with 10 digits are typically in seconds, while 13-digit timestamps are in milliseconds. Our timestamp converter automatically detects the format and converts accordingly for accurate results.

faq.q: Does the timestamp converter handle different time zones?
faq.a: Yes, our timestamp converter can display results in different time zones and accounts for daylight saving time changes. This ensures accurate conversions regardless of your geographic location.

faq.q: What's the valid range for timestamp conversion?
faq.a: The timestamp converter supports timestamps from 1970 to 2038 for 32-bit systems, and extends much further for 64-bit timestamps. This covers virtually all practical use cases for modern applications.

faq.q: Can I convert current time to timestamp?
faq.a: Yes, our timestamp converter includes a current timestamp generator that provides the current Unix timestamp in both seconds and milliseconds formats. Perfect for real-time applications and testing.

faq.q: Is the timestamp converter useful for developers?
faq.a: Absolutely! The timestamp converter is essential for developers working with databases, APIs, log files, and any system that uses Unix timestamps. It simplifies debugging and data analysis tasks significantly.
